terms.meaning: A written task on the team's board, with an owner and a status.
terms.analogy: A sticky note on a kitchen order rail: what to make, who is making it, and whether it is done.
terms.example: ORD-14: Rename the checkout button to Place order.

terms.meaning: A board of columns that shows every ticket and how far along it is.
terms.analogy: The order rail in a restaurant kitchen, with columns for waiting, cooking, plating and served.
terms.example: To do, In progress, Review and Done.

terms.meaning: The folder that holds a project's code together with its full history of changes.
terms.analogy: A shared recipe book that remembers every edit anyone ever made.
terms.example: The Bowlful app lives in one repository on GitHub.

terms.meaning: Your own copy of the code to work on, separate from what everyone else is using.
terms.analogy: Photocopying a page of the shared notebook so you can scribble on it without touching the original.

terms.meaning: The branch that holds the team's agreed, working code. What goes live comes from here.
terms.analogy: The master recipe that the restaurant actually cooks from.
terms.example: A change reaches customers only after it is merged into main.

terms.meaning: A saved snapshot of your changes, with a short message saying what changed.
terms.analogy: Saving a numbered version of a document, with a note on what you edited.
terms.example: ORD-14 Rename checkout button to Place order
terms.command: git commit -m "ORD-14 Rename checkout button to Place order"
terms.shortcut: Ctrl+Enter in the VS Code source control message box

terms.meaning: Bring the newest changes from GitHub into your copy.
terms.analogy: Checking the shared notebook for new pages before you start writing.
terms.example: Marcus added a delivery fee while you were away; a pull brings it to you.

terms.meaning: Send your commits from your computer up to GitHub so others can see them.
terms.analogy: Handing your finished pages to the team's shared folder.
terms.example: Your branch appears on GitHub after you push it.

terms.meaning: The usual name for the shared copy of the repository on GitHub.
terms.analogy: The master notebook that lives in the team office, while yours is a copy on your desk.
terms.example: git pull origin main means: pull main from the shared copy.

terms.meaning: A request to add your branch's changes to main, which also opens a place for tests and review.
terms.analogy: Handing in your homework for a teacher to check before it goes in the class book.
terms.example: PR #1: ORD-14 Rename checkout button to Place order.

terms.meaning: A teammate reads your change and either approves it or asks for edits.
terms.analogy: A second cook tasting the dish before it leaves the kitchen.
terms.example: A reviewer approves the PR after reading the one-word change.

terms.meaning: Small programs that check, in seconds, that the code still does what it should.
terms.analogy: A checklist the kitchen runs on every plate before it is served.
terms.example: A test checks that the checkout button says Place order.

terms.meaning: Combine the changes from one branch into another.
terms.analogy: Taping your edited page back into the shared notebook.
terms.example: Merging your PR adds your branch's commits to main.

terms.meaning: Git cannot combine two changes because two people edited the same lines differently.
terms.analogy: Two people erased and rewrote the same sentence in the same notebook.
terms.example: You and Marcus both changed the delivery fee line.

terms.meaning: An agreement on what a request and a response look like, so frontend and backend can build at the same time.
terms.analogy: The order form both the waiter and the kitchen agree on before service starts.

terms.meaning: Release the new version so real users get it.
terms.analogy: Putting the new dish on the menu after it passes the taste test.
terms.example: After the merge, the live Bowlful app shows Place order.
